lead: World Heritage monuments, neighbourhoods with centuries of history, Mediterranean nature and Spain’s most renowned cuisine. Everything Valencia has to offer.

Valencia is much more than Fallas and beaches. The capital of the Turia treasures an extraordinary monumental heritage, from jewels of civil Gothic to a futuristic complex that has redefined contemporary Spanish architecture.
We have selected the 10 must-see places in Valencia from the best travel guides: UNESCO monuments, protected natural areas and neighbourhoods with a unique identity that no visitor should miss.

items.title: Valencia’s futuristic icon
items.body: The great cultural complex designed by Santiago Calatrava in the old Turia riverbed brings together the Oceanogràfic, the Museu de les Ciències and the Hemisfèric, with the largest 3D cinema screen in Spain.

items.title: Plaza de la Virgen, Cathedral and Miguelete
items.body: The monumental heart of Valencia. Beside the Basilica of the Virgen de los Desamparados and the Cathedral rises the Miguelete, the Gothic bell tower with the best views of the historic centre.

items.title: Church of San Nicolás: the Valencian Sistine Chapel
items.body: Nicknamed the Valencian Sistine Chapel, this 14th-century Gothic church dazzles with vaults covered in 17th-century Baroque frescoes. Almost 2,000 square metres of breathtaking painting.

items.title: La Lonja de la Seda: World Heritage Site
items.body: The crowning work of 15th-century Valencian civil Gothic and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Its slender helical columns and the light filtering through its windows make it one of the most beautiful corners of the city.

items.title: Central Market: a temple of Modernisme and gastronomy
items.body: One of the largest food markets in Europe, with more than 250 stalls beneath a Modernista dome of 8,000 m². Declared an Asset of Cultural Interest and the ideal setting for the traditional Valencian esmorzaret.

items.title: Plaza Redonda and Santa Catalina tower
items.body: One of the most singular squares in Spain: perfectly circular and reached from four different streets. From here you can see the Baroque tower of Santa Catalina, one of the most photographed bell towers in Valencia.

items.title: El Carmen district and the Serranos Towers
items.body: Valencia’s most vibrant medieval district: little streets with street art, the IVAM, the Centre del Carme and the Portal de la Valldigna. At its ends stand the Serranos and Quart Towers, the only gates left of the 15th-century walled city.

items.title: Turia Gardens: 9 km of urban park
items.body: Valencia’s green lung runs along the old riverbed for nine kilometres, free of cars. Historic bridges, sports areas, the Bioparc and the Gulliver park make this space an essential walk on foot or by bike.

items.title: El Cabanyal: the seafaring soul of Valencia
items.body: A fishing district declared a Protected Historic Ensemble, with a unique popular Modernisme in its tiled façades. Bohemian, gastronomic and authentic: the perfect counterpoint to the historic centre.

items.title: L’Albufera Natural Park: paella and sunset over the lake
items.body: One of the most important wetlands of the Iberian Peninsula, just ten kilometres from the centre. Rice fields, virgin dunes, pine forests and the great lake where you can discover the origin of Valencian paella aboard a traditional albufera boat.

blocks.title: Practical tips for visiting Valencia
items: The València Tourist Card includes transport and discounts at monuments
La Lonja de la Seda and San Nicolás require advance booking online
The Central Market closes on Sundays and public holidays
For the Albufera, take bus 24 or 25 from the centre
The Miguelete closes at midday: visit it first thing
El Cabanyal is a must for dinner: book in advance
